Read the whole paper before it is due.
Give him extra time to finish the paper.
Choose a topic for him this week.

questions.s: What is the student's problem?
questions.e: She says 'it's the wrong edition' and her syllabus requires the tenth, while she has the ninth. She does have her receipt, and the clerk says the right book is in stock.
o: She lost the receipt for her purchase.
She bought an old edition of the book.
The book costs too much for her budget.
The store has no copies of the book left.

questions.s: What does the student decide to do?
questions.e: She says 'I'd like to exchange it,' and the clerk explains she must pay the difference. A refund was offered, but she chose the exchange.
o: Get her money back.
Keep the book and borrow another one.
Exchange the book and pay extra.
Come back with her teacher.

questions.s: Why does the woman talk to the man?
questions.e: She asks 'Is it too late to join?' The rest of the talk is about how the club works and what to bring. The poster is only how she heard about the club.
o: She wants to complain about a poster that is wrong.
She wants to borrow equipment for a long trail.
She wants to find out how to join the club.
She wants to plan a trip to her hometown.

questions.s: What does the man say about the Saturday trip?
questions.e: He says 'Our trips are for all levels' and 'it's an easy walk.' The bus leaves at eight in the morning, and membership costs ten dollars, so the other choices are wrong.
o: It is suitable for beginners.
It is a long and difficult hike for experienced walkers.
It begins in the afternoon after the club meeting.
It is free for everyone who brings their own lunch.

questions.s: What is the main purpose of the supervisor's talk with Amara?
questions.e: He says 'I wanted to talk about your first week' and then praises her work and plans training. The training is on Wednesday afternoon, but he does not ask her to stay late.
o: To ask her to stay late on Wednesday.
To discuss how she is doing at work.
To tell her the internship is ending soon.
To explain how to use the company software.

questions.s: What will Amara probably do after the training?
questions.e: The supervisor says 'afterwards, we'll give you your own project... a small campaign for the spring sale.' The other actions are never suggested.
o: Teach the marketing team how to use social media.
Ask for a longer internship with the company.
Work on a small campaign by herself.
Write a report about the training session.

questions.s: What is the conversation mainly about?
questions.e: Sofia complains about dirty dishes, and they agree on a cleaning schedule. Money and noise are not discussed.
o: Buying new dishes for the apartment.
Paying the rent on time each month.
Finding a quieter place to sleep.
Sharing the kitchen cleaning.

questions.s: What does the man mean when he says 'Thanks for being patient with me'?
questions.e: He has just agreed that he left dishes undone, and he thanks her for waiting for him to change. This shows he knows the problem was partly his fault.
o: He wants to change his practice time.
He knows he should have helped more.
He thinks the woman is too slow at cleaning.
He plans to move out of the apartment soon.

questions.s: What does the woman want to know?
questions.e: Her first words are 'I need to get to the city airport. Which train should I take?' Her suitcases are the reason she wants a direct train, not the question itself.
o: How to travel to the airport.
Where to leave her heavy suitcases.
When the station will close tonight.
How much a taxi to the city costs.

questions.s: Why does the woman choose the airport express?
questions.e: She asks for a direct train because she has two big suitcases, and the express is direct. The express runs only every hour, so the last choice is wrong, and the price is not compared.
o: It is much cheaper than the blue line.
It leaves from a platform near the machine.
It needs no change of trains.
It runs every few minutes through the day.

questions.s: Why is the man at the gym?
questions.e: He says 'I just started classes, and I'd like to join.' He is taking a tour and filling in a membership form.
o: To apply for a job at the front desk.
To ask about becoming a member.
To sign up for a swimming race.
To return a student card he found.

questions.s: What does the man say about the price?
questions.e: He says 'That's cheaper than I thought.' The woman lists the weight room, pool and group classes, so the price covers more than two things.
o: It is higher than at other gyms he has seen.
It is too expensive for a student to pay.
It includes only the weight room and the pool.
It is lower than he expected.

questions.s: Why did the man come to the health center?
questions.e: He says 'I've had a sore throat for three days, and now I have a cough too.' No injury, vaccine or sports form is mentioned.
o: He needs a form for a sports team.
He wants a vaccine before his trip abroad.
He hurt his arm during a class.
He has been sick for days.

questions.s: What does the nurse recommend?
questions.e: She says 'Mostly rest and plenty of water' and offers throat tablets. She says he may attend class if he feels better, so a full week at home is too extreme.
o: Rest, drink water, and use throat tablets.
Take strong medicine and avoid all classes for a week.
See a doctor in the city this afternoon.
Eat more food and exercise every morning.

questions.s: What does the woman want to find out about the soup?
questions.e: She asks 'Does the soup have any meat in it? I don't eat meat.' The man mentions butter and freshness on his own, but those are not her question.
o: Whether it costs less than the salad.
Whether it contains meat.
Whether it is served with butter.
Whether it was made today.

questions.s: What problem does the woman have at the end?
questions.e: She says 'I left it in my room,' meaning her meal card, and asks to pay with cash. The man says cash is accepted, so money is not the problem.
o: She does not have enough cash to pay.
She cannot find a table to sit at.
She forgot her meal card.
She ordered the wrong kind of soup.

questions.s: Why did the student come to see the professor?
questions.e: He says 'I got a lower grade than I expected.' The rest of the conversation is about how to improve his writing.
o: He was disappointed with a grade.
He missed class and needs the notes.
He wants to change to a different course.
He hopes to become her research assistant.

questions.s: What does the professor suggest the student do?
questions.e: She says 'try writing an outline first' to 'organize your points before you start.' She does not offer a rewrite of the old essay; her advice is for the next assignment.
o: Rewrite the last essay for a better mark.
Stop writing essays at night completely.
Choose easier topics for his assignments.
Plan his essay before he writes it.

questions.s: What are the speakers mainly doing?
questions.e: Aisha says 'We need to decide who does which part,' and they divide the research and the slides. The topic is never discussed.
o: Complaining about a difficult professor.
Deciding who will do each task.
Choosing a topic for their presentation.
Looking for a new member for their group.

questions.s: What does Chen say he is worried about?
questions.e: He says 'I'm not great at speaking in front of people.' He likes finding information, and he says Thursday works, so the other options do not fit.
o: Speaking in front of other people.
Finding enough information for the research.
Missing the meeting on Thursday.
Making the slides look attractive.

questions.s: What was the man's problem?
questions.e: He says 'someone was already inside' the room he reserved. The worker finds that his booking was for 4B, not 4A, so he simply went to the wrong room.
o: He forgot to make a reservation.
He could not log in to the library system.
He thought his study room was taken.
He arrived two hours late.

questions.s: What can be inferred about the man's feeling at the end?
questions.e: He says 'I must have gone to the wrong room. I feel silly,' which shows embarrassment. The worker reassures him that 'It happens a lot,' and his two hours are safe.
o: He is angry at the person in the other room.
He feels a bit embarrassed.
He is worried that he will lose his booking.
He is surprised that the library is so busy.

questions.s: What does the woman want to learn about?
questions.e: She says she's 'thinking about moving off campus' and asks about the apartment list. Her dorm is only mentioned as a price comparison.
o: Housing off campus.
Rules for living in the dorm.
Ways to find a part-time job.
Prices at the campus bookstore.

questions.s: What does the man point out about the cost?
questions.e: He says 'you'll also pay for electricity and internet,' meaning the rent does not cover them. The woman says the rent is less than the dorm, so the first wrong choice is reversed.
o: The apartments are more expensive than the dorm.
Students must pay a full year in advance.
The rent includes electricity and internet.
Bills for utilities are paid separately.

questions.s: What is the woman's main concern?
questions.e: She says 'I have a lab at ten, and I'm already running late,' so she is worried about time. Fares and friends are never mentioned.
o: Finding her student card.
Getting to her lab on time.
Paying the correct bus fare.
Meeting a friend at the north gate.

questions.s: What does the driver suggest she do?
questions.e: He says 'you should take the number eight bus' and tells her to catch it across the street. Walking from the north gate is what this bus offers, but the number eight is faster.
o: Take a different bus across the street.
Walk to the north gate from the next stop.
Wait for the next bus on this route.
Call the science building for directions.

questions.s: What is the conversation mostly about?

o: Buying a better camera.
Planning a trip to a museum.
A first club meeting.
Choosing a photo for a contest.

questions.e: He says 'I'd love to show my work, but I'm not sure my pictures are good enough.' That mixes interest and doubt. Nobody mentions a fee.
o: Interested but unsure of his skills.
Eager because his pictures are already excellent.
Uninterested because he prefers indoor photos.
Upset that members must pay to take part.

questions.s: Why does the man meet with the coordinator?

o: To report a problem at his workplace.
To ask about courses for next term.
To volunteer at the school library.
To get help with an application.

questions.e: She says 'put that near the top' about his volunteer experience, since it 'shows you can work with the public.' She wants the resume on Monday, not next year.
o: Apply to a different museum.
Put his library work first.
Wait until next year to apply.
Take a course about museums first.

questions.s: Why does the man speak to the woman?

She left the lights on in the hall.
Her music is keeping him awake.
She woke him up with a phone call.

Go to bed right away.
Ask the man to join her.
Buy headphones tonight.

A set of colored pencils.
A gift for his teacher.
A sketchbook for class.

The first one is too small for class.
The clerk gives him a free bag.
His teacher asked for two books.

To change her appointment time.
To submit her project proposal.
To complain about the lecture.

It should be at least ten pages long.
The details are available online.
She will present it to the class.

To book a visit for his back.
To find out where the clinic is.
To cancel a soccer practice.

He prefers to see a different doctor.
He is busy on Thursday.
He needs time to fill out forms.

She wants to compete in a race.
She lost a bet with the man.
Her doctor advised it.

Running on the treadmill longer.
Asking the doctor for another plan.
Joining him at the library later.

Balancing classes and a job.
Paying for tuition next semester.
Finding a roommate for the fall.

Quitting the cafe job entirely.
Taking six classes in the fall.
Graduating a semester later.

He cannot find a book.
He is late for the library.

Ask the librarian to print for him.
Go to class without his essay.
Wait for the printers to be free.

To report a broken heater.
To choose a meal plan.

She plans to cook in her room.
It costs too much for her budget.
It does not include the cafe.

He has too much reading to finish.
He disagrees with the course topic.
He forgot to buy the textbook.

Read each page more slowly.
Study with a friend each night.
Read the main parts first.

A problem on the train.
Their plans today.

It is not very popular.

Help starting a program.
A new locker for his bag.
Advice on healthy cooking.

The heavy machines are broken.
He wants to lose weight quickly.
He once hurt his shoulder.

To exchange a book she damaged.
To ask about online prices.

Angry enough to refuse it.
Upset but accepting.
Unsure how much she paid.

She is interested in a job.
She needs help with a statistics test.
She missed his class on Monday.

o: Go to an interview.
Start entering data.
Take a spreadsheet exam.
Attend his class at two.

o: The cost of groceries.
A broken refrigerator.
Food taken by mistake.
Plans for a dinner party.

He wants the same shelf as her.
They are about the same height.
Neither one owes the other.

He played as a child.
He won a national prize.
He teaches younger students.

It is the same as other clubs.
It covers a new board.

To ask for a refund.
To find a platform.
To change her travel date.

o: The Saturday fare is cheaper.
She missed her original train.
A family event came up.
She wants a different seat.

The lunch menu.
A student discount.
A table by the window.

questions.e: After hearing the discount lasts all term, he says he will come more often. That implies the cheaper price makes the cafeteria attractive.
o: The price now suits him.
He plans to work in the cafeteria.
He likes the juice more than the sandwich.
He lost his campus card before.

Find sources.
Print an old article.
Meet her professor.

o: They are shorter and easier to read.
Her professor wrote most of them.
They can be printed for free.
Experts check them first.

She is getting a new job here.
She wants a bigger room.
She will stop her classes.

o: Introduce her cousin to the landlord.
Look at other apartments.
Learn whether her plan is final.
Help the man pack.

o: Too much exercise.
Little sleep and water.
A problem with his eyes.
Loud noise in his room.

questions.e: He says it right after being told to sleep seven hours. It shows he fears the exams will keep him from sleeping more. The doctor replies about short breaks.

He hopes to stop the headaches by Friday.
He is unsure when the clinic is open.
He worries he cannot follow the advice.

questions.s: Why does the man go to the bus station?

o: To get back a lost bag.
To buy a monthly pass.
To ask about a late bus.
To report a stolen laptop.

questions.e: She asks 'what else is in it?' and he lists a notebook, water bottle and keys, which 'matches.' The bus number alone could not prove it.
o: He shows his student card.
She calls the bus driver.
He lists its contents.
He knows the bus number.

questions.e: She says she's 'struggling to find recent research' and the books are old. She already has a topic, so the last choice is wrong.

Borrowing books from the nineties.
Choosing a topic for her project.
Locating up-to-date sources.

Read the older books closely.
Cite a few classic studies.
Ask her professor for articles.

Results he did not expect.
He did not finish the lab report.
His hypothesis was too simple.

They are probably wrong and must be redone.

They are better than perfect data.

To apply for a room in Oak Hall.
To ask about a closure of his dorm.
To get a letter from his department.

The size of the room in Pine Hall.
Meeting a new roommate.
Getting a letter in time.

Which classes are the most difficult.
Why Hamza is so tired.
Where to buy a calendar.

It made her work worse.
It is a good way to finish early.
It requires a calendar app.

He lost his membership card.
He plans to end his membership.

Refuse to change the policy.
Charge him for the extra week.
Give him a form to sign.

She needs a recommendation letter.
She disagrees with a grade.

It is easier than the other topic.
The student cares more about it.
He studies small towns himself.

His book order is late.
He cannot afford the book.
His email address is wrong.

He plans to write in the new book.
He will buy the book at another store.
He accepts a used copy for now.

To buy a new computer together.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A how-question about the past needs a past-tense reply. The reply about next week uses the future.
o: It was great. We went to the lake.
I will go to the lake next week.
Weekends are on Saturday and Sunday.
Yes, it was in the morning.
questions.sy: W: How was your weekend?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Handing over a pen answers the request. The others describe a pen or a past use.
o: I borrowed one from him yesterday.
Sure, here you go.
My pen is a blue one.
I wrote a letter with it last night.
questions.sy: M: Do you have a pen I can borrow?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A where-question needs a place. The reply with 'I will put them in the car' has the wrong tense.
o: I will put them in the car.
Yes, the keys are very small.
On the kitchen table.
I put on a warm coat.
questions.sy: W: Where did you put the keys?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Accepting the apology and saying the start was recent is polite. The others are rude or irrelevant.
o: The meeting ended late yesterday.
You should leave earlier next time.
The train was at eight o'clock.
That's okay. We just started.
questions.sy: M: I'm sorry I'm late.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Accepting the offer is the polite reply. The others describe the bags without answering.
o: Thanks, that would be great.
The bags are heavy because of the books.
I carried them yesterday, too.
Bags are on sale at the mall.
questions.sy: W: Can I help you carry those bags?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The speaker hints that he is cold. Offering heat is the natural reaction.
o: Yes, I was cold last winter.
I'll turn on the heater.
The cold drink is on the table.
It is a very old building.
questions.sy: M: It's getting cold in here.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question is yes/no about the past. The reply about finishing at school today is in the future, and the others are a different topic.
o: No, I will finish it at school today.
Homework is very difficult for me.
Yes, I did it after dinner.
It is in my blue bag, I think.
questions.sy: W: Did you finish your homework?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The speaker suggests sharing, so agreeing with a reason fits. The others change the subject or use the wrong tense.
o: The airport is next to the hotel.
No, I took a taxi last year.
I want a plane ticket to Dubai.
Good idea. It will save money.
questions.sy: M: Do you want to share a taxi to the airport?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A complaint about the food is best met with a fix. The others ignore the problem.
o: Let me add some water.
Yes, the soup is in the pot.
I eat soup on Sundays.
Salt is cheap at the shop.
questions.sy: W: This soup is too salty.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question is about the speaker's plans, so a plan answers it. The other choices talk about the past or give general facts.
o: No, the party was great last week.
Yes, I'll be there at eight.
I like parties with good music.
Friday is the fifth day of the week.
questions.sy: M: Are you coming to the party on Friday?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Advising rest and tea responds to the complaint of feeling sick. The others repeat "cold" without advice.
o: Yes, it is very cold today.
I had a cold last month.
You should rest and drink tea.
Tea is grown in many countries.
questions.sy: W: I think I have a cold.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A request for directions needs directions. The others use words like post or tell but answer other questions.
o: Yes, I sent it by post.
The office opens at nine.
I told him about it last week.
Go straight, then turn left.
questions.sy: M: Can you tell me how to get to the post office?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "Not at all, go ahead" answers the polite request. The others talk about the music without giving permission.
o: Not at all, go ahead.
I downloaded the playlist last night.
The music starts at seven tonight.
It's a new album from my favorite band.
questions.sy: W: Do you mind if I turn the music down?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Agreeing and saying you have to leave soon shows a shared reaction. The others state unrelated facts or misuse the idea.
o: The meeting room is on the second floor.
Me too. I have to leave soon.
It was held on Monday morning.
I thought so, so I brought a snack.
questions.sy: M: I thought the meeting would be shorter.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Telling where to look answers the question. The others repeat "glasses" without helping.
o: Yes, my sister wears glasses too.
I saw those on sale at the mall.
Try the table by the sofa.
I haven't been to the optician yet.
questions.sy: W: Have you seen my glasses anywhere?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Agreeing and asking where to go accepts the suggestion. The others use the wrong tense or give irrelevant facts.
o: The restaurant was closed last night.
I ate out at noon yesterday.
Tonight is the first night of Eid.
Sounds good. Where shall we go?
questions.sy: M: Why don't we eat out tonight?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Showing interest and asking which course responds to the plan. The others repeat "course" without responding.
o: That sounds useful. Which one?
I took a computer course last year.
The last course finished at five.
Courses are very expensive in the capital.
questions.sy: W: I'm thinking of taking a computer course.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Apologizing and asking for another table is the polite reply. The others ignore the problem.
o: Yes, we reserved a table for four.
Oh, sorry. Is another free?
It is a very nice table by the window.
We ate here a week ago.
questions.sy: M: Sorry, but this table is reserved.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'How long have you lived' asks for a duration up to now. The reply with 'until June' looks to the future.
o: I will live here until June.
It is a big and busy city.
About three years now.
Yes, I live near the park.
questions.sy: W: How long have you lived in this city?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Agreeing and asking where it goes responds to the request. The others describe the box or use the wrong tense.
o: The box is made of thick paper.
I gave it to you yesterday.
I can't find the other boxes.
Sure. Where does it go?
questions.sy: M: Could you give me a hand with this box?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Offering to check responds to the tag question. The others talk about a past viewing or the length.
o: I think so. Let me check.
Yes, I saw it with my sister.
It lasted about two hours, I think.
The cinema is next to the market.
questions.sy: W: The film starts at seven, doesn't it?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Asking for the receipt is the next step in a return. The others misread "return" or comment on the shirt.
o: It looks good on you, though.
Do you have the receipt?
We return from our trip at noon.
I bought a similar shirt last week.
questions.sy: M: I'd like to return this shirt.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Offering to look it over responds to the worry. The others do not offer help.
o: Fridays are always busy for me.
I reported the problem to the manager.
Do you want me to look it over?
You finished the last one on Thursday.
questions.sy: W: I'm not sure I can finish this report by Friday.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A surprised reaction and a plan respond to the news. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, I heard the news on the radio.
The cafeteria has really good coffee.
It closed at six yesterday, I think.
Really? I'll eat first.
questions.sy: M: Did you hear that the cafeteria is closing early?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Choosing walking with a reason answers the question. The others do not choose.
o: Walking. I need the exercise.
The bus is usually late on Fridays.
I took the bus here yesterday.
I really liked the walk we took.
questions.sy: W: Would you rather take the bus or walk?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Agreeing and sharing a money-saving tip responds to the complaint. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, the textbooks are on the second shelf.
I know. I buy mine used.
I think that one costs ten dollars.
I read that chapter last week.
questions.sy: M: I can't believe how expensive textbooks are.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Saying you will check the schedule responds to the request. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: I worked the Saturday shift last month.
The shift ended on time yesterday.
Let me check my schedule first.
Saturday is the best day to shop.
questions.sy: W: Is there any chance you could cover my shift on Saturday?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Explaining the reason answers the remark. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, the exercise was very hard today.
I looked at the schedule for an hour.
You look pretty tired yourself.
I was up all night with the baby.
questions.sy: M: You look exhausted.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Admitting uncertainty and suggesting asking responds to the question. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: It's hard to say. I'd ask her.
Yes, she extended it last semester too.
The deadline is printed in the syllabus.
I think she is grading the papers now.
questions.sy: W: Do you think the professor will extend the deadline?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Sharing the surprise and giving a reason responds to the remark. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, I expected you to be here.
Same here. Visiting a friend.
I'll see you later this week.
I come to this library every day.
questions.sy: M: I didn't expect to see you here.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Offering to call someone responds to the problem. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, I printed my paper on it this morning.
I printed it on Wednesday.
I'll call someone to fix it.
The printer costs a lot to repair.
questions.sy: W: The printer is jammed again.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Saying they post it online answers the question. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, I know the lecturer well.
It was recorded last semester.
The lecture hall holds two hundred people.
I think they post it online.
questions.sy: M: Do you know whether the lecture is recorded?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Offering to split the bill is the polite counter. The others use the wrong tense or ignore the offer.
o: Thanks, but let's split it.
You were swamped last week, too.
Yes, dinner was on me yesterday.
I'll be free tomorrow until noon.
questions.sy: W: I'm swamped this week, so dinner is on me tomorrow.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Reassuring the speaker is the polite reply. The others blame them or change the topic.
o: You should have called me yesterday.
No worries. It happens to everyone.
I called, but nobody answered then.
Yes, I meant to call you, too.
questions.sy: M: I meant to call you, but it slipped my mind.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Suggesting an advisor responds to the uncertainty. The others misread being "on the fence".
o: I'm glad you finally made up your mind.
Yes, you should have switched last year.
Maybe talk to an advisor first.
I changed mine two years ago, too.
questions.sy: W: Honestly, I'm on the fence about changing majors.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Agreeing and saying you learned a lot responds to the remark. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: It was held in the main auditorium.
Yes, I'm opening the next session at noon.
The presentation started at noon.
I learned a lot from it, too.
questions.sy: M: That presentation was a real eye-opener for me.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Offering to ask for another copy responds to the problem. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Then I'll ask them to order one.
The copy machine is on the third floor.
I'm afraid I haven't read it yet.
Yes, I returned the book yesterday.
questions.sy: W: I'm afraid the library just ran out of copies.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Accepting that and arranging another way responds to the explanation. The others misread the offer.
o: Thanks, I'll ride with you tomorrow.
No problem. I'll catch the bus.
Yes, the shop sells nice cars.
I'd offer you a ride if I could.
questions.sy: M: I'd offer you a ride, but my car's in the shop.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Explaining what is on your mind responds to the concern. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, the meeting was at ten.
I have been working here since March.
Just thinking about my workload.
Quiet places are good for study.
questions.sy: W: You've been quiet since the meeting. Everything okay?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Politely disagreeing while keeping the confidence responds well. The others betray the confidence or ignore the remark.
o: I'll tell everyone right away.
The schedule was printed last night.
Yes, I'm sure it will be a great success.
I see your point, but give it time.
questions.sy: M: Between us, I think the new schedule is a mistake.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Proposing a coffee break responds to the wish. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Let's grab a coffee, then.
You could use my notes, too.
The last break was ten minutes long.
Yes, studying is a lot of work.
questions.sy: W: I could use a break from all this studying.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'A lot on my plate' means too many duties. Advice about cutting something fits. The others are literal.
o: Yes, the plates are in the cupboard.
Maybe drop one of your clubs.
I ate a lot at the restaurant.
The semester ends in December.
questions.sy: M: I've got a lot on my plate this semester.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Correcting the date answers the tag question. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, I handed mine in this morning.
The deadline was long enough.
No, it's next week now.
Today is my sister's birthday, actually.
questions.sy: W: Wasn't the deadline supposed to be today?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Thanking someone for being a good sport responds to the reluctant agreement. The others take "cup of tea" literally.
o: I prefer coffee in the morning.
Yes, I'll make you a cup of tea.
You'd better go quickly, or you'll miss it.
Thanks for being a good sport.
questions.sy: M: It's not exactly my cup of tea, but I'll go.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Agreeing and asking about the deadline responds to the request. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Glad to. When is it due?
I read it twice in the morning.
The essay was about climate change.
Yes, I hope you get a good grade.
questions.sy: W: I was hoping you could proofread my essay.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Realizing the earlier deadline and starting now responds well. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, I drafted it at noon yesterday.
Then I'd better start now.
I wanted a different professor.
Midnight is when the library closes.
questions.sy: M: The professor wants the draft by noon, not midnight.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Admitting uncertainty and suggesting the website responds to the question. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, the holiday is next Monday.
I happen to love that gym.
Not sure. Check the website.
It opened last year in spring.
questions.sy: W: Do you happen to know if the gym is open on holidays?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'Running low on patience' signals frustration. Offering support fits. The others take running or low literally.
o: Our project is in the green folder.
I'm also running low on coffee today.
The group meets on Thursday afternoons.
Want me to talk to them with you?
questions.sy: M: I'm running low on patience with this group project.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A headache here means a nuisance. Encouraging patience fits. One reply takes it literally.
o: Give it a week. It gets easier.
You should take some medicine for it.
Yes, the software is sold in the campus store.
I installed it a bit later than you.
questions.sy: W: This new software is a bit of a headache.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The speaker declines politely, and the reply understands and offers an alternative. The others repeat afraid, able or talk.
o: Yes, I'm nervous about public speaking.
That's fine. I'll send my slides.
The talk is in the main hall at six.
You could have told me last week.
questions.sy: M: I'm afraid I won't be able to make it to your talk.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The polite request is met with a willing offer. The others misread trouble or move.
o: Yes, it would be too much trouble.
My appointment is on a day off.
Not at all. Which day suits?
I moved to a new place last week.
questions.sy: W: Would it be too much trouble to move my appointment?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A complaint about repeated lateness leads to a practical adjustment. The others twist third or late.
o: The third bus is always the most crowded.
It was late on the third of May, too.
The bus schedule changes next week.
Let's leave earlier tomorrow.
questions.sy: M: That's the third time the bus has been late this week.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question asks for a time, and "At nine, I think" gives one. "Yes, I read it" mixes up "closes" and "read"; the floor answers "where", not "when".
o: Yes, I read it last night.
It's on the second floor of the main building.
No, I closed the window already.
At nine, I think.
questions.sy: W: Do you know when the library closes tonight?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "Where" asks for a place, so "on the kitchen table" fits. The reply about last Tuesday gives a time, not a place.
o: It's on the kitchen table.
I put it away last Tuesday afternoon.
Yes, I wrote it in my notebook.
My notebook is blue and has a long cover.
questions.sy: M: Where did you put my notebook?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A polite request is best answered by doing it. "Yes, I could eat" repeats "could" and "salt" but ignores the request.
o: Yes, I could eat some more salt.
Salt is bad for your health, you know.
Here you go.
I couldn't find the pepper in the kitchen.
questions.sy: M: Could you pass me the salt, please?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The man shares good news, so a congratulation is natural. Advice to study more is socially odd, and the other replies ignore what he said.
o: I think the exam starts at ten o'clock.
That's great news. Congratulations!
You should study chemistry more often.
Which exam did you take yesterday morning?
questions.sy: M: I got an A on my chemistry exam!

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The man offers a ride, so accepting politely is best. "I rode my bike" uses the wrong tense, and the other replies only repeat "home" and "class".
o: I rode my bike to class today.
Yes, my home is near the river.
The class ends at five fifteen.
That would be great, thanks.
questions.sy: M: Would you like a ride home after class?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "How long" asks for a length of time, and "About fifteen minutes" gives it. The other replies talk about habit, appearance, or a past event.
o: I walk to campus every single day.
It's a long road with many trees.
About fifteen minutes.
Yes, it took me an hour once.
questions.sy: M: How long does the walk to campus take?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: After an apology, the natural reply accepts it and suggests a solution. The others repeat "forgot", "bring" and "book" without answering.
o: Yes, I forgot to buy a new book.
No problem. Bring it tomorrow.
The book is about the history of Rome.
I'll bring a book to the party.
questions.sy: W: I'm sorry, I forgot to bring your book.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "When" asks for a time, so "At seven" fits. The past-tense reply and the place answer different questions, and "Yes" does not suit a "when" question.
o: At seven in the morning.
It opened last year, I think.
Yes, the gym is open on Saturday.
The gym is behind the stadium.
questions.sy: W: When does the gym open on Saturday?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The woman has a problem, so a helpful question is natural. The replies that talk about a new card, the price or a found card do not help her.
o: Did you check your backpack?
Yes, I have a new card too.
The card costs about ten dollars.
I found it in front of the school.
questions.sy: W: I can't find my student card anywhere.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The man invites her, so accepting and asking for details is best. Past dinner and the place do not answer an invitation.
o: I had dinner at six last night.
Yes, the dinner was really delicious.
I'd love to. What time?
It's near the train station downtown.
questions.sy: M: Would you like to join us for dinner tonight?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A yes or no question about opening is answered by "Yes, from ten to four." The other options use the wrong tense, describe the pool, or talk about something else.
o: I swam there last Sunday, actually.
Yes, from ten to four.
The pool is very deep at one end.
No, I don't have a swimsuit today.
questions.sy: W: Is the swimming pool open on Sundays?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: He asks for help, so agreeing and starting to explain is best. The others use the past tense, give a place, or avoid the request.
o: Yes, I scanned it yesterday at noon.
The scanner is in the library lobby.
I use my phone to take photos.
Sure. Press the green button first.
questions.sy: M: Can you show me how to use this scanner?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "How did it go" asks for an evaluation of a past event. The future reply has the wrong tense, and the topic answers "what", not "how".
o: I'll give it on Thursday afternoon.
Pretty well. They liked it.
It was about climate and rainforests.
Yes, the room was very cold.
questions.sy: W: How did your presentation go?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: When someone apologizes, forgiving is a polite response. The other options either repeat the word "cup" or change who broke it and when.
o: Don't worry. It was an old one.
Yes, I bought a new cup yesterday.
Please buy a new cup at the store.
I broke it when I was a child.
questions.sy: M: I'm sorry, I broke your cup.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A thank-you is answered with "You're welcome." The other options repeat "homework" or "help" without responding to the thanks.
o: Yes, my homework is on the desk.
I have homework in math and history.
You're welcome. Anytime.
I need some help with math too.
questions.sy: W: Thanks for helping me with my homework.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "Why" asks for a reason, and the free lunch is a reason. The others answer where, whether, or how often.
o: It's on the first floor, next to the gym.
Yes, the cafeteria is open until three.
I eat lunch there almost every day.
There's a free lunch for new students.
questions.sy: M: Why is the cafeteria so crowded today?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: An "or" question needs a choice. "Tea, please" chooses one; "Yes" does not choose, and the past-tense option talks about another time.
o: Yes, I want a coffee and a tea.
I wanted to go to the cafe yesterday.
Tea, please. I had coffee already.
The coffee machine is broken again.
questions.sy: W: Do you want coffee or tea?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The man reports a problem, so offering to tell someone is helpful. The other options talk about scanning in general and do not deal with the problem.
o: Yes, I scanned my paper there.
The lab opens at nine every morning.
It works better than my old scanner.
I'll tell the lab assistant.
questions.sy: M: The scanner in the lab isn't working.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "How much" asks for a price. The bookstore answers where, and the pages answer a different question about size.
o: I bought it at the bookstore.
It's two dollars and fifty cents.
It's a notebook with a hundred pages.
Yes, I need a new notebook too.
questions.sy: W: How much is this notebook?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question is about a future plan. The correct reply says what she wants and what stops her. The others use past tense or give general information.
o: I'd like to, but I have a shift.
Yes, the study room was very quiet.
Wednesday is the middle of the week.
We studied together last Wednesday.
questions.sy: M: Are you free to study together on Wednesday?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "Which bus" asks for a bus number. The reply "number twelve" answers it. A yes answer does not fit a "which" question.
o: The stadium is very big and busy.
I went to the stadium last month.
Take number twelve, over there.
Yes, the bus goes there every day.
questions.sy: W: Which bus goes to the stadium?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The man complains he is tired, so a sympathetic suggestion is natural. The other options repeat "midnight" without caring about his tiredness.
o: You should get some rest, then.
Yes, I study at midnight too.
The test will be at twelve o'clock.
I usually go to bed at ten.
questions.sy: M: I'm so tired. I studied until midnight.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The woman asks about location, so "across the street" gives it. The others repeat "pharmacy" but talk about products, a cold, or a past time.
o: No, the pharmacy sells many medicines.
Yes, there's one across the street.
I need some medicine for my cold.
The pharmacy closed at eight last night.
questions.sy: W: Is there a pharmacy near here?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question is about the past, and "Almost" answers it honestly. The others are about the essay's topic, the wrong time, or a different word.
o: Yes, the essay is about the weather.
I will finish the essay next week.
No, I didn't see the finish line.
Almost. I'll finish this morning.
questions.sy: M: Did you finish the essay last night?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The woman asks to use a calculator, so agreeing and handing it over is the right reply. The others repeat words but do not respond.
o: Sure, here you go.
It's a minute past two now.
Yes, my calculator is in a box.
I bought it at the school store.
questions.sy: W: Can I use your calculator for a minute?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The man complains about the noise, and closing the door is a practical response. The other replies ignore the comment.
o: Yes, the class begins at nine.
The classroom is on the third floor.
I noticed the noise yesterday, too.
Let's close the door.
questions.sy: M: It's so noisy in this classroom.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "What did you think" asks for an opinion. The correct reply gives one. The others describe the length, the future, or the place.
o: It's a two-hour movie at the cinema.
I liked it. The ending was funny.
Yes, I will see the movie tomorrow.
The movie theater is next to the bank.
questions.sy: W: What did you think of the movie?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "Who" asks for a person's identity or role. The others talk about clothes, which only repeats the words from the line.
o: She is wearing blue shoes today.
Yes, I wear a jacket in winter.
That's our new English teacher.
The jacket costs about forty dollars.
questions.sy: M: Who is the woman in the blue jacket?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "Have you ever" asks about experience, so "Yes, I jog there" answers it. The future reply and opening hours do not answer the question.

The park is open from six to ten.
No, I was at home in the park.
Yes, I jog there on weekends.
questions.sy: W: Have you ever been to Lakeside Park?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The man asks for directions, so "down the hall, on the left" fits. Registering for classes and closing time answer different questions.
o: Yes, I registered for three classes.
It's down the hall, on the left.
The office closes at four thirty today.
I told her where the office was.
questions.sy: M: Could you tell me where the registration office is?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The woman has a problem, and offering a charger helps. The other options talk about laptops in general but do not offer help.
o: You can use my charger.
Yes, I have a new laptop too.
The battery lasts about ten hours.
Laptops are very useful these days.
questions.sy: W: My laptop battery is almost dead.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "Do you mind" is answered "Not at all" when you agree. "Yes, I read" repeats the word "read" but does not answer.

I usually read in the library.
Not at all. Go ahead.
The street was noisy this morning.
questions.sy: M: Do you mind if I sit here and read?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "How often" asks about frequency, so "Three times a week" fits. Yesterday's hour is about one time, and the gym is a place.
o: I exercised for an hour yesterday.
Yes, exercise is very good for health.
Three times a week, usually.
At the gym on Main Street.
questions.sy: W: How often do you exercise?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: He shares good news, so congratulating and asking a follow-up question is natural. The other replies pick up the word "bookstore" only.
o: Yes, I read many books last year.
The bookstore is open on Sundays too.
I will buy a book there tomorrow.
Congratulations! When do you start?
questions.sy: M: I just got a job at the bookstore.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A yes or no question about habit. "No, I usually walk" answers it. The others use "train" but give a platform, a past event, or a destination.
o: No, I usually walk.
Yes, the train is at platform two.
I took the train yesterday evening.
It's the train to the city center.
questions.sy: W: Do you take the train to school?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question asks about plans, so "Nothing special" answers it. The others use past tense or give general information about weekends.

Nothing special. Why do you ask?
Yes, the weekend is two days long.
It's a weekend in the middle of May.
questions.sy: M: What are you doing this weekend?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The speaker lost something, so suggesting a next step is helpful. The others mention the wallet or taxi but do not help.

The taxi was full of people today.
I bought my wallet at that store.
Let's call the taxi company.
questions.sy: W: I think I left my wallet in the taxi.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: An "or" question needs a choice. "On Tuesday" chooses one. The last option repeats both days but gives no answer.

The exam was very difficult for us.
It's on Tuesday, I believe.
I studied on Monday and Tuesday.
questions.sy: M: Is the history exam on Monday or Tuesday?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The waiter offers a seat, so accepting politely is best. The other options misunderstand the offer.

Yes, I'd like that. Thank you.
The window is made of thick glass.
The window in my room faces the street.
questions.sy: W: Would you like to sit by the window?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The man shares news, and a surprised reaction fits. The other replies mix up "closed" with other meanings.
o: No, I didn't. That's too bad.
The pool is very popular in summer.
The pool closes at ten tonight.
I swim there every Saturday.
questions.sy: M: Did you know the pool is closed for repairs?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "Where" asks for a location, so "inside the bank" works. Needing money is a reason, not a place.

Yes, ATM stands for a machine.
It was open at seven yesterday.
There's one inside the bank.
questions.sy: W: Where's the nearest ATM?

questions.s: Choose the best response.

Let me take a look at it.
The homework is on page fifty.
I had a problem with my car.
questions.sy: M: I'm having trouble with this science homework.

questions.s: Choose the best response.

No, I ate soup yesterday.
The restaurant opens at noon.
It costs five dollars a bowl.
questions.sy: W: The soup here is really good, isn't it?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The customer asks politely, and the waiter agrees. The other replies repeat "bill" or "could" but do not respond to the request.

We have a table for four people.

I could not read the menu.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: She offers to shop, so naming something is natural. The past-tense reply and the distance answer different questions.

I went to the supermarket on Friday.
The supermarket is far from here.

questions.sy: W: I'm going to the supermarket. Do you need anything?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The man complains, and a helpful question is a natural response. The other options repeat "night" without responding to the problem.

He always wakes up at seven.
The night is very quiet here.
Have you talked to him?
questions.sy: M: My roommate is always so noisy at night.

The dessert is made in the kitchen.
It's a menu with four pages.

In June, on the twentieth.
She wore a white dress last year.

questions.s: Choose the best response.

Five pounds is about two kilograms.
You should eat more vegetables.

questions.sy: W: I've lost five pounds this month!

Yes, the science class is hard.
The building was built in 1990.
I get to school by bus.
questions.sy: M: Excuse me, how do I get to the science building?

The door is painted dark green.

How about a scarf?
The gift shop closes at six.
I bought a gift last week.
questions.sy: M: I need to buy a gift for my mother.

I'm from the university downtown.

I've lived in this city for two years.

I usually go to the library.

He moved here in January.
The neighbors have a large garden.

The pizza costs ten dollars.
It was cold last winter.

The restaurant is very good value.
I ate at a restaurant last week.

The dentist was very kind to me.
Three is my lucky number today.
Then you should leave soon.
questions.sy: M: I have a dentist appointment at three.

I visited Boston last summer.

It's a matter of five dollars.

By bike, when it's dry.

It opens at nine in the morning.
The third floor.

I'm going to visit my cousins.

My plans are on the kitchen wall.

Tomorrow is Thursday, isn't it?

The class meets on Tuesday and Thursday.

I was a student there last year.

I sit here every day, thanks.
The seat is too hard for me.

The account is very expensive.
I closed my account last month.

The afternoon starts at noon.

Monday is the first day of class.
My class is at ten o'clock.
I was sick with the flu.

The break lasts about ten minutes.
I take a bus to my workplace.
Good idea. I'll make some tea.

The tables are in the cafeteria.
No, you can join us.
I sat here for twenty minutes.

I left the station at ten.

Yes, I looked at the garden today.
The library has a very big garden.
Books are good for the mind.

It's about two dollars.
The bus comes every ten minutes.
The ticket cost her a lot of money.

The bed is too small for me.

I don't have any classes today.

questions.s: Choose the best response.

It rained a lot on Sunday.

questions.s: Choose the best response.

Salt comes from the sea.
The soup is served with bread.

The arm has three main bones.
I fell off my bike.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The customer asks for a change. The clerk agrees and checks. The others repeat "seat" without helping.

I like to sit near my friends.

I know the teacher well.
It was six when I got home.

The dinner was very good last night.

The bookstore sells cheap notebooks.
I walked there two years ago.

questions.s: Choose the best response.

Good idea. I know a nice cafe.
Eating too much is not healthy for you.
The cafe closes at three.

questions.s: Choose the best response.

The ticket cost me ten dollars.
Here it is.
I may go there next week.

The morning is the best time to study.
You should see a doctor.
I felt dizzy on the bus yesterday.

Reading is a good habit for children.
It's a book about the school.
A mystery novel by a local writer.

The show lasts about two hours.
Saturday is the busiest day of the week.

o: I'm going to the salon on Monday.
The barber shop is closed today.
Thanks. I finally got tired of the old one.
Yes, I've been meaning to buy a hat.
questions.sy: M: Is that a new haircut? It looks great.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: "I wouldn't count on it" answers the question about opinion. The others use the wrong tense.
o: Yes, the snow was deep last winter.
They canceled it last year, I think.
It snowed more than this last winter.
I wouldn't count on it.
questions.sy: W: Do you think they'll cancel class because of the snow?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Giving the time left answers "When". The others give a past event, a place, or the wrong tense.
o: We have about twenty minutes.
I had lunch with her yesterday.
The cafeteria is on the first floor.
Lunch was served an hour ago.
questions.sy: M: I'm starving. When's lunch?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Sympathizing responds to the complaint. The others change the topic or criticize.
o: I made a sandwich for the trip.
That's rough. At least you made it.
Traffic is always light on weekends.
You should have left earlier, then.
questions.sy: W: I got caught in a traffic jam on the way here.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Agreeing and starting with goggles responds to the request. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: I walked through the lab on Monday.
The safety office is down the hall.
Of course. First, always wear your goggles.
Yes, I read the rules last year.
questions.sy: M: Could you walk me through the lab safety rules?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Agreeing to bring the pot responds to the request. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: The coffee shop opens at seven.
Yes, I filled out the form yesterday.
Refills are free if you buy a mug.
Absolutely, I'll bring the pot over.
questions.sy: W: Could I get a refill on my coffee, please?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Agreeing that it is time responds to the news. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: About time. That place was falling apart.
I tore my jacket in the old gym.
I heard about it from the neighbors.
They tore the gym down yesterday morning.
questions.sy: M: I heard they're tearing down the old gym.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Choosing to stay with a reason answers the question. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: I headed out early last night.
Let's stay until the band finishes.
The band is playing a new song now.
I'd like a little more time to rest.
questions.sy: W: Do you want to head out or stay a little longer?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Thanking and saying you will be right out responds to the news. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, I interrupted the lecture last night.
I'm sorry, I didn't ask for a ride.
Thanks. Tell him I'll be right out.
The ride takes about an hour.
questions.sy: M: Sorry to interrupt, but your ride is here.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Confirming with a note about the time answers the question. The others reuse words from the line, use the wrong tense or person, or answer a different question.
o: Yes, I took the class last spring.
The class costs ten dollars.
No, yoga is in the next building.
You're a bit early, but yes.
questions.sy: W: Is this the right place for the yoga class?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The speaker reports a delay, so proposing to follow up fits. The others reuse transcript or registrar words without responding to the problem.
o: Then let's ask them to chase it up.
Yes, I requested my transcript last month.
The office is closed on public holidays.
I registered for four courses this term.
questions.sy: W: The registrar's office told me my transcript hasn't arrived yet.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'Going back and forth' means undecided. Asking about his instinct responds to the dilemma. The others miss the point.
o: I think the team meets on Wednesdays.
What does your gut tell you?
Debates are held in the east building.
I joined the choir a month ago.
questions.sy: M: I've been going back and forth on whether to join the debate team.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A long shot is an unlikely success. Encouraging the attempt is the sensible reaction. The others are literal or irrelevant.
o: The scholarship was awarded in April.
I applied for a similar one last year.
Good for you. Why not?
Yes, the deadline for it is next Friday.
questions.sy: W: It's a bit of a long shot, but I'm applying for the scholarship anyway.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The speaker admits he is behind. Urging him to start fits. The others reuse lab, Monday or start in unrelated ways.
o: The lab report is worth thirty percent.
I reported the broken equipment to the lab manager.
It's not due until the end of the month.
Then get cracking tonight.
questions.sy: M: The lab report was due Monday, and I haven't even started.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'I don't suppose you could' is a polite request. Agreeing and promising action fits. The others ignore it.
o: Sure, I'll scan them tonight.
I suppose Tuesday was a busy day for everyone.
Yes, I lent them to Mina last week.
I took very few notes on Tuesday.
questions.sy: W: I don't suppose you could lend me your notes from Tuesday.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The remark shows he is stressed. Sympathy fits. One reply contradicts him with an unrelated claim.
o: The department is in the technical building.
I can imagine. Hang in there.
It has been rather quiet, actually, in my lab.
The department hired two new people.
questions.sy: M: Things have been a bit hectic at the department lately.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'Nothing to write home about' means unremarkable. Comforting her fits. The others take the idiom literally.
o: I'll send the final draft home next week.
Yes, the second draft is due on Friday.
That's fine. First drafts rarely shine.
I appreciate your honesty, but I disagree.
questions.sy: W: I'll be honest, the first draft was nothing to write home about.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A delay affects the hotel arrival, so informing them is the helpful reaction. The others miss the consequence.
o: The new route goes through the mountains.
Yes, the landing was smooth last time.
The flight attendants were very polite.
I'll tell the hotel now.
questions.sy: M: Our flight got rerouted, so we'll land three hours late.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The speaker is annoyed. Asking what happened is the natural next step. The others miss the emotion.
o: What happened? Did he break something?
You should lend it to me instead.
Yes, that laptop is the lightest model made.
That was the last bus I took home.
questions.sy: W: That's the last time I lend him my laptop.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: He expresses surprise, so confirming the news with a time fits. The others change tense or meaning.
o: Yes, I'm aware of next week's seminars.
It was called off this morning, I think.
The dean can cancel it without notice.
Seminars are usually held on Fridays.
questions.sy: M: I wasn't aware the seminar had been cancelled.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The line gives advice. Accepting the advice and showing agreement fits. The others twist the grammar or ignore it.
o: If I were you, I'd have signed it already.
Yes, I signed it with a black pen.
Good point. I won't rush.
Opinions about contracts vary in each country.
questions.sy: W: If I were you, I'd get a second opinion before signing.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: He hopes for good weather. A shared wish plus a forecast fits. The others misuse hold or field.
o: Yes, the weather was great last time.
The field was very wet last June.
The trip costs fifteen dollars each.
Fingers crossed. Forecast's good.
questions.sy: M: I'm hoping the weather holds out for the field trip.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'Run something by you' means share an idea. Inviting her to go on fits. The others take run or minute literally.
o: Sure, go ahead. I'm all ears.
Yes, I run about a mile every morning.
I ran the numbers yesterday, and they look fine.
I already bought you lunch today.
questions.sy: W: Do you have a minute? I need to run something by you.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The line is a piece of news. Reacting with surprise and a follow-up question fits. The others twist step down.
o: Yes, the dean was at the ceremony yesterday.
Really? Who's taking over?
The year ends in December, right?
I saw the dean in the cafeteria this morning.
questions.sy: M: Apparently the dean is stepping down at the end of the year.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: She is disappointed. Sympathy and a practical question fit. The others use heart, set or room in unrelated ways.
o: Corner rooms are cheaper in the north.
I had my heart set on a trip to the coast.
Too bad. Is there another?
The room set came with a very nice table.
questions.sy: W: I had my heart set on the corner room, but it's gone.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The speaker delays a permit. Accepting and adapting fits. The others ignore the delay, mention the wrong time or reply as if it were ready.
o: Then I'll pick it up on my way home tonight.
Last week the permit office moved to the annex.
I'd rather park in the visitor lot than walk.
That's fine. I'll walk until then.
questions.sy: M: I'm afraid the parking permit won't be ready until next week.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A complaint about group effort leads to a plan of action. The others deny the problem or only restate the situation.
o: Let's call a meeting and sort it out.
I'm glad that everyone cares so much about it.
Our group got a better grade than the others.
It seems that the group project is due soon.
questions.sy: W: Our group is falling behind, and nobody seems to care.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: It is a compliment, so a modest thanks fits. The others misread the praise as a question or a plan.
o: I'll have the recipe sent to you tomorrow.
Thanks. I was a little nervous.
You should have invited the other guests, too.
Dinner will be served after the guests arrive.
questions.sy: M: You really outdid yourself with this dinner.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question asks whether the reading was clear. An honest 'not really' fits. The others answer length, timing or location.
o: Yes, it was about two hundred pages long.
I'll read it again on Thursday afternoon.
Not really. Maybe the lecture helps.
The reading list is posted on the course site.
questions.sy: W: Were you able to make sense of the reading for Thursday?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: An excuse is met with understanding. The others criticize, contradict or talk about prices.
o: You should charge your phone every single night.
I did call you twice, but nobody answered then.
Earlier calls are cheaper on the weekend plan.
No worries. Things happen.
questions.sy: M: I'd have called earlier, but my battery died.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'Can't thank you enough' is strong gratitude and a polite 'don't mention it' answers it. The others add facts without accepting thanks.
o: Don't mention it. Anytime.
You're welcome to borrow my truck next week.
It took us about four hours in total.
I moved to this city two years ago as well.
questions.sy: W: I can't thank you enough for helping me move.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: He wants rest, and agreeing fits. The others suggest busy plans or ignore his wish.
o: Then let's go to the concert on Saturday night.
Same here. Let's not plan anything.
The weekend market is always very noisy and crowded.
I could do the report on Sunday afternoon.
questions.sy: M: Honestly, I could do with a quiet weekend.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The speaker is cold and asks for confirmation. Agreeing fits. One reply disagrees without logic, and the others change topic.
o: I think the lecture starts at ten past nine.
It's fine for me. Maybe sit by the window?
It's not just you. I'm freezing.
The lecture halls were built in the nineteenth century.
questions.sy: W: Is it just me, or is it freezing in this lecture hall?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A remark about a quiet colleague invites a charitable explanation. The others state facts about meetings or compare himself to her.
o: Meetings are held each morning at nine thirty.
I think she was hired to speak to clients.
I hardly said a word in my first week, either.
Maybe she's just shy. Give her time.
questions.sy: M: The new hire barely says a word in meetings.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'Keep it down' means be quieter. Apologizing and moving fits. One reply answers 'mind' wrongly, and the others ignore the request.
o: Oh, sorry. I'll take this outside.
No problem. I never mind a bit of noise.
Sure, I'll keep the key down at the front desk.
I concentrate best in the early evening hours.
questions.sy: W: Would you mind keeping it down? I'm trying to concentrate.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Both are surprised by short notice, so agreeing fits. The others give content, blame him or use the wrong time.
o: The quiz covers chapters four and five only.
Same here. No warning.
You should have checked the website earlier.
I found the answers in the library yesterday.
questions.sy: M: I only found out about the quiz this morning.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question asks what else to bring. A concrete item answers it. The others stay on the passport, give a past story or mention snacks.
o: Your passport must be valid for six more months.
Some visitors bring snacks for the long flight.
Just a printout of your confirmation.
I brought everything the last time I travelled.
questions.sy: W: Is there anything else I should bring besides my passport?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: He says he dislikes mornings, so proposing a later time fits. The others ignore his preference.
o: Then you will love the early shift at seven.
I usually wake up around six thirty each day.
That is a good reason to sleep until noon.
Neither am I. Let's meet after lunch.
questions.sy: M: I'm not much of a morning person, to be honest.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: An older edition may differ, so asking if it works is the useful question. The others skip that issue or add side facts.
o: Is that one close enough to use?
I'll order the newest edition from them online.
The bookstore opens at eight on Saturdays only.
Older books are often cheaper than new ones.
questions.sy: W: The bookstore only had the older edition left.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: He realizes an oversight. Helping fix it fits. The others blame him, add a comment or talk about timing.
o: You should have read the whole form earlier.
It's easy to miss. Let's fix it now.
Two signatures make the process much longer.
I signed my part right after I got it.
questions.sy: M: It never occurred to me that the form needed two signatures.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question asks about plans. Mentioning a pending letter implies he may be delayed. The others answer a different time or contradict.
o: Yes, I submitted the one from last year.
The deadline for this program is quite strict.
I'm still waiting on a reference letter.
No, I have never filled out an application.
questions.sy: W: Are you planning to submit the application before the deadline?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'Leaning toward' answers with a tentative choice. The others use the wrong time or give general facts.
o: I decided to take the elective bus home.
Electives are worth three credits each term.
Yes, last term I took geology as well.
I'm leaning toward the geology one.
questions.sy: M: Have you decided which elective to take next term?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question is an offer to share a fare. Checking for cash is a natural answer. The others are unrelated or past.
o: Let me see if I have cash.
The cab driver took the main highway.
Costs are lower during the daytime hours.
I split a cab with them last week.
questions.sy: W: Do you want to split the cost of the cab?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question asks about arrival. A scheduled time implies it has not come yet. The others twist ship and arrive.
o: Yes, the supplier was shipped last month.
It's supposed to be here by noon.
The shipment weighs more than a ton.
I arrived early at the warehouse today.
questions.sy: M: Has the shipment from the supplier arrived yet?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A polite refusal with a reason answers the invitation indirectly. The others use the wrong tense or topic.
o: The study session was extremely helpful.
Tonight's weather is supposed to be mild.
I wish I could, but I have a shift.
I made it to the last one on time.
questions.sy: W: Can you make it to the study session tonight?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question asks for an opinion, and a mild criticism gives one. The others state facts about the event.
o: The speaker was invited by the dean.
I think the talk starts at four o'clock.
Guests are expected to sit near the front.
It ran a little long for my taste.
questions.sy: M: What did you think of the guest speaker's talk?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The tag-like question checks the deadline. Explaining an extension answers it indirectly. The others twist survey or supposed.
o: I got an extension until Friday.
Yes, I surveyed the whole building today.
I'm supposed to be on holiday this Friday.
The survey took me about ten minutes.
questions.sy: W: Weren't you supposed to hand in the survey today?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question asks for a prediction. A conditional reply expresses doubt. The others use the past or mention facts.
o: I think the experiment lasted for two hours.
Only if the samples cooperate.
We finished the last one in the evening.
The time was set by the lab technician.
questions.sy: M: Do you think we'll finish the experiment in time?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question asks about distance. An approximate walking time answers it. The others offer price, view or a wrong sense of close.
o: Campus housing is cheaper than apartments.
The apartment has a view of the harbor.
It's a ten-minute walk, give or take.
Yes, I closed the door when I left.
questions.sy: W: Is the apartment close to the campus?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: It is a request to substitute. A conditional agreement fits. The others misuse present or answer a different question.
o: I was able to present on Monday morning.
Presents are usually wrapped in plain paper.
Monday is when the department meets, right?
Give me the slides and I'll try.
questions.sy: M: Would you be able to present in my place on Monday?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question asks whether it was fixed. A partial answer says it was not. The others stay on kitchen or landlord facts.
o: He sent someone, but it's still dripping.
The kitchen is the largest room in the flat.
Yes, I leaked the story to my landlord.
The landlord lives in a house near the park.
questions.sy: W: Did the landlord ever fix the leak in your kitchen?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'How come' asks for a reason. Missing the train gives one. One reply gives a contradictory motive and the others avoid the question.
o: The train goes directly to the north side.
I missed it by about a minute.
Early trains are always fairly crowded here.
I took the later one because I wanted to.
questions.sy: M: How come you didn't take the earlier train?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The question assumes a choice. 'Neither' with a reason gives a surprising but direct answer. The others avoid it.
o: I ended up at the airport that day.
Both apartments have large windows and light.
Neither. The rent was out of range.
The two apartments are on different floors.
questions.sy: W: Which of the two apartments did you end up choosing?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A who-question needs a person or group. The others give a place, advice or a yes/no reply.
o: The workshop is on the third floor.
Resumes are best kept to one page.
Yes, I give workshops all the time.
Someone from career services.
questions.sy: M: Who's giving the workshop on resume writing?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: A how-much question needs a rough amount. The others answer other questions.
o: I think it's about two hundred dollars.
The registration form is online right now.
The conference took place in Toronto once.
Costs depend on how you travel there.
questions.sy: W: Do you know how much the conference registration costs?

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The idiom means working too hard. Advising rest fits. The others take burning literally or add unrelated facts.
o: The candle shop opens at nine on weekdays.
You should take it easy before you burn out.
Midterms always start in the second week of March.
I burned a candle during the power cut last night.
questions.sy: M: I've been burning the candle at both ends since midterms started.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'Spill the beans' means reveal a secret. A reaction to the ruined surprise fits. The others are literal.
o: Beans are a healthy food for the party.
The party was a surprise to every guest.
Oh no. Now we'll have to plan something else.
He spilled the drinks on the carpet yesterday.
questions.sy: W: He spilled the beans about the surprise party.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: Being up to one's ears means very busy. Offering help fits. The others take it literally.
o: Yes, I filed my paperwork in the office.
I wore earplugs during the entire flight.
This week's paper is up on the website.
Want me to take some of it?
questions.sy: M: I'm up to my ears in paperwork this week.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'Piece of cake' means very easy. A contrasting personal reaction is natural. The others are literal.
o: Lucky you. I found it pretty tough.
Cake is served after the exam in the hall.
Yes, I baked a cake for the teacher.
The exam papers have to be returned on Monday.
questions.sy: W: That exam was a piece of cake.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: 'In the same boat' means sharing a situation. Proposing joint action fits. The others take it literally.
o: Boats are not allowed on the university lake.
True. Let's all talk to him.
I rented a small boat for the weekend.
Yes, the rent was increased by a quarter.
questions.sy: M: We're all in the same boat when it comes to rent increases.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: She implies problems. Asking what went wrong follows. One reply contradicts her, and the others miss the point.
o: I'd say it went better than last year's.
Yes, I would say it was a good project.
What went wrong? Was it the budget?
The project was approved in the spring.
questions.sy: W: I wouldn't say the project went smoothly.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: He complains that he was forced. Sympathetic agreement fits. The others generalize, point to a rule or blame him.
o: I'll make a choice by Friday.
This kind of matter is covered in the handbook.
You chose to go there last winter, though.
I know. It wasn't fair to you.
questions.sy: M: It's not like I had a choice in the matter.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: The speaker voices a criticism in confidence. A fair, measured response fits. The others take depth literally.
o: Let's give her the benefit of the doubt.
I think she's been doing a great job so far.
Between us, I think there are only two managers.
I heard she moved here from another branch.
questions.sy: W: Between you and me, the new manager seems out of her depth.

questions.s: Choose the best response.
questions.e: He accepts a loss gracefully. Encouragement fits. The others play on shot.
o: We lost by about two points, didn't we?
There's always next season. Chin up.
